growth_problem.statement: The growth problem in Venezuela is a slowdown since 2014 (-8.5 percent a year over the last decade against 0.7 in the decade before). GDP per capita growth over 2016–2025 averaged -8.5 percent a year (2006–2025: -3.9; no structural-peer median), with no convergence residual available and ranked 1 of 1 among structural peers. GDP per capita peaked in 1977, 48 years ago, and is 70.4 percent below that peak; a peak older than 30 years is context here, not the growth problem. GDP per capita is lower than in 1960, the first year of the record. Since 1990 growth has run in three eras: 1990–2003 at -1.0 percent a year, 2004–2013 at 4.4 and 2014–2025 at -8.1. Investment (gross fixed capital formation to GDP) relative to expectation given income cannot be computed at 4.2 percent of GDP; the private-public split is unavailable in prototype (IMF Investment and Capital Stock Dataset not ingested). Gross savings relative to expectation given income cannot be computed; the current account balance is 1.0 percent of GDP and net FDI inflows are -1.2 percent of GDP. Structural change (G9) is not computed in the prototype. Exports to GDP relative to expectation given income cannot be computed. The relevant question is therefore: why has growth slowed since 2014, and what stopped investment from sustaining it. Provisional top-split reading: indeterminate (no statistic available; not available: the real lending rate, real private credit growth, the investment residual).
